"You have all been granted citizenship! I have the papers here!" The Flora broke out in a big cheer.

"Some of you may like living in the city, some may not. Is this true?" The Flora murmured in agreement.

The crater and city was named Kureta by popular vote of the Flora. It meant crater in their ancient language, Mar'dy didn't think it was particularly creative to call it Crater but he wasn't going to protest.

The crater had developed deep gullies and rills from the rain water and rivers feeding into it. In the center was an island surrounded by a freshwater lake. The gullies were loaded with bits of the sentinels, sometimes even meters thick, providing an easy source of metals for the colony. The rock was blasted apart in workable pieces of limestone and within a few days, makeshift homes started to pop up. The ground was rich with minerals from the ground and nitrates formed by the massive energy explosion. For the next few years the soil would amazingly productive, allowing the Flora to plant farms and forests in this crater with relative ease. It was a perfect location. He would stay with the Flora for the next while, sorting out problems as he could, writing acquisition forms from Sentenza and parcelling out land deeds for the Flora. Lately I have noticed an influx of old news being posted. This ranges from a month, to a year, to several years. But each time

  • It receives upvotes from people who like the content (which says nothing about whether it violates the rules, just to be clear. For all we know, the upvoaters don't even read the article)

  • Anyone who points out that it's old news is downvoted

  • The aforementioned people are treated as "enemies" who aren't opposed to the content because it's not /v/news material, but because they personally don't like the content. I.e. if I report a submission of old news about cops being dumb, it's not because I dislike old news submissions on /v/news, but because I am a cop fanboy who thinks they can do no wrong.

And just to point out that it's not a rare phenomenon, I see 2 on the front page right now:

  • https://voat.co/v/news/comments/848546 - Article is from a year ago

  • https://voat.co/v/news/comments/848462 - Article is from 2013

2 out of 25 isn't bad, right? Well going by that logic, 3 out of 25 would be okay too, and 4, and 5, and so on... eventually, this sub could mainly be a place to fuel agendas and manipulate others. For instance, say I love Hilary Clinton and hate Donald Trump. Under the current ruleset, I'm allowed to submit old articles that portray her in a good light, and him in a bad one. Since both these people are presidential candidates, it's relevant to today, right? Hopefully my example shows why Rule 1 needs to be refined or changed entirely - in its current state it is just way too exploitable, and has no way to control quality.
